exposure: General Anaesthesia (thiopentone sodium 6 mg/kg and succinyl choline 1.5 mg/kg)
outcome: Hemodynamic parameters (heart rate, SBP, DBP, MAP)
Neonatal outcomes (birth weight, APGAR score at 1 and 5 minutes)
cohort: The study included 60 pre-eclamptic parturients undergoing elective cesarean sections, divided into two groups based on the type of anaesthesia received.
finding: Spinal Anaesthesia resulted in better hemodynamic stability, patient awareness, postoperative analgesia, and good neonatal outcomes compared to General Anaesthesia for pre-eclamptic parturients undergoing elective cesarean section.
followup_time: 5 minutes after birth (for neonatal APGAR score)
gest_age: Comparable between two groups (specific values not provided)
